questions.explanation: Morphine is the principal opium alkaloid derived from the opium poppy, Papaver somniferum.

questions.question_text: Ion exchange chromatography is the method of choice for separation of -
questions.explanation: Ion exchange chromatography is widely used for the separation and analysis of ionized species such as metal ions.

questions.question_text: Rideal Walker test is performed by using the strain -
questions.explanation: The Rideal-Walker coefficient test evaluates disinfectants using Salmonella typhi as the standard test organism.

questions.question_text: Tetracycline undergo epimerization C-4 between pH 4 and 8 to give -
questions.explanation: Reversible epimerization of tetracyclines at the C-4 position yields epitetracyclines in mildly acidic to neutral pH ranges.

questions.question_text: Tyndalisation means -

options.D: Successive autoclaving at low temperature and incubator

questions.explanation: Tyndallization involves fractional sterilization by successive heating at low temperatures to kill vegetative cells and spores.

questions.question_text: Morphine and heroin differ from each other in respect of -

options.C: Abesence of double bond between $C_4$ and $C_6$

questions.explanation: Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is formed by the acetylation of morphine's hydroxyl groups at positions $C_3$ and $C_6$.

questions.question_text: Vincristine and Vinblastine act by -

options.A: Binding with the protein tubulin and arrest at metaphase

questions.explanation: Vinca alkaloids bind to tubulin, inhibiting microtubule formation and arresting cells at metaphase.

questions.question_text: A rhamno-glucoside on complete hydrolysis will give -
questions.explanation: A rhamno-glucoside contains rhamnose and glucose sugars bound to an aglycone, yielding aglycone, rhamnose, and glucose upon complete hydrolysis.

questions.question_text: The technique employed to study the insoluble film at oil water interface is -
questions.explanation: A film balance is used to study insoluble monolayers and surface films at interfaces.

questions.question_text: Gray baby syndrome is due to the indiscriminate use of -
questions.explanation: Gray baby syndrome is a serious adverse reaction associated with high systemic levels of chloramphenicol in neonates.

questions.question_text: $N,N$ dimethyl -(1-methyl-1-oxo-3,3-diphenylhexyl) ammonium chloride is the chemical -
questions.explanation: Darvon (propoxyphene related compound nomenclature or derivative descriptor) matches this chemical description.

questions.question_text: Sulphonamide tragedy was due to combination with -
questions.explanation: The 1937 Elixir Sulfanilamide disaster involved the toxic solvent diethylene glycol (often referred loosely or mistranslated in texts as diethylene hydrochloride variants).

questions.question_text: In the preparation of tablets, powdered medicaments are mixed by -
questions.explanation: Powder mixing ensures content uniformity and reduces interparticle segregation.

questions.question_text: One nanometer ($nm$) is equal to -
Cholinergic receptor present on intestinal muscle is -
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic control of intestinal smooth muscle is mediated by muscarinic (specifically $M_3$) cholinergic receptors.

questions.question_text: Indicate the correct order of increasing eluent power of benzene, ether, chloroform and ethyl acetate-
questions.explanation: Eluent strength on normal-phase silica increases generally from non-polar benzene to moderately polar ether, chloroform, and ethyl acetate.

questions.question_text: Limulus test is rapid in vitro test for parentrals to detect the presence of -
questions.explanation: The Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) test is used to detect bacterial endotoxins (pyrogens) in parenterals.

questions.question_text: An essential requirement of the mobile phase in HPLC is that -

options.A: It must have constant flow rate with pulses
options.C: It must be run at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ only

questions.explanation: HPLC mobile phases must be properly prepared, degassed, and pure (often freshly prepared/distilled and filtered) to avoid column fouling.

questions.question_text: Indian (Tinnevelly) and Africa seena leaves differ from other with respect to -
questions.explanation: Different species of senna (Cassia angustifolia vs. Cassia auriculata/obovata) differ in microscopic constants like vein-islet number, stomatal index, and morphological color.

questions.question_text: 3-Etherification of morphine molecules causes -
questions.explanation: Masking the phenolic hydroxyl group at C-3 via etherification (as in codeine) reduces analgesic potency and addictive liability compared to morphine.

questions.question_text: Addition of electrolyte to a lysol may cause -
questions.explanation: Adding electrolytes to soap solutions/lysol causes precipitation of soap micelles, commonly referred to as salting out.

questions.question_text: Salicin, a phenolic glycoside, on hydrolysis yields -
questions.explanation: Salicin is hydrolyzed into D-glucose and saligenin (salicyl alcohol).

questions.question_text: Lignocaine hydrochloride is officially assayed by -
questions.explanation: Salts of weak organic bases like lignocaine hydrochloride are officially assayed using non-aqueous titration.

questions.question_text: In supra ventricle arrthymia Digoxin when supplemented with __ is dangerous -
questions.explanation: Co-administration of calcium with digoxin can precipitate severe cardiac arrhythmias due to synergistic effects on intracellular calcium overload.

questions.question_text: Injection of insulin I.P. should be kept at PH between -
questions.explanation: Neutral or slightly acidic solutions (pH around 7.0 for neutral regular insulin, or pH 5-5.5 for stability in certain formulations) maintain insulin stability.

questions.question_text: Some adrenocorticoids are referred to as $\Delta$-corticoids because of -

options.A: High amount of unsaturation in the molecules
options.B: Additional double bond in ring A between carbon 1 and 2
options.C: Presence of one double bond in each ring
options.D: Absence of double bond in ring A

questions.explanation: Delta-corticoids (like prednisolone) possess a $\Delta^{1,2}$ double bond (an additional double bond between carbons 1 and 2 in ring A).

questions.question_text: In radioactive pharmaceuticals half life of compound means -

options.A: The time taken for one half of the compound to find with serum albumin
options.B: The time taken for onset of its action
options.C: The time taken for the activity to decay to one half of its inhinitial value
options.D: The time taken for its complete metabolism

questions.explanation: Radioactive half-life is defined as the time required for the radioactivity of a specified isotope to decay to half its initial value.

questions.question_text: Wagner's test is used to detect the presence of -
questions.explanation: Wagner's reagent (iodine in potassium iodide) is a standard precipitation test used to detect alkaloids.

questions.question_text: Metronidazole inhibits anaerobic bacteria and protozoa by -

options.A: Affecting the structure of DNA molecule of the organism

questions.explanation: Metronidazole is reduced by anaerobic microbial proteins, forming reactive intermediates that damage microbial DNA.

questions.question_text: Most comman oesterogen progesterone preparation used as oral contraceptive agent contains -
questions.explanation: Common oral contraceptives combine an estrogen (ethinyl estradiol) and a progestin (norethindrone or similar derivatives).

questions.question_text: Before washing the ampoules the mouth of each ampoule is rotated in Bunson flame to melt down the rough edge .This process is called as -
questions.explanation: Flaming or fire polishing is the process of heating glass ampoule necks to smooth sharp or rough edges.

questions.question_text: In Benzothiadiazides reduction of the double bond between the position 3 and 4 gives rise to -
questions.explanation: Saturation of the 3,4-double bond in benzothiadiazides (thiazide diuretics) yields hydrothiazides, which possess significantly higher diuretic potency.

questions.question_text: Peripheral neurotransmitter is -
questions.explanation: Noradrenaline is a primary peripheral neurotransmitter of the sympathetic nervous system.

questions.question_text: Beer's laws state that -

options.A: Absorbance of a solution is indirectly proportional to the absorbing solute
options.B: Absorbance of a solution is indirectly proportional to the length of cell
options.C: Absorbance of a solution is directly proportional to the absorbing solute
options.D: Transmittance of a solution is directly proportional to the absorbance solvent

questions.explanation: Beer's law states that absorbance is directly proportional to the concentration of the absorbing species in solution.
